newsitem.title: USA: EchoStar amends suit, seeks financing.
newsitem.headline: EchoStar amends suit, seeks financing.

text.p: Satellite-dish TV firm EchoStar Communcations Corp on Monday said it amended a breach-of-contract suit against media giant News Corp, further unraveling a $1 billion investment deal that the companies signed in February.
EchoStar said it seeks damages resulting from News Corp's "many uncured material breaches" of the agreement, including "lost profits" it said could exceed $5 billion.

EchoStar said that because of News Corp's alleged failure to meet its obligations, which includes a $200 million loan, it cannot fulfill its business plan. EchoStar said it has consulted investment banking firms, regarding methods of meeting its capital needs.
EchoStar said it intends to speak with major vendors and other potential strategic partners. It said it believes it can arrange transactions to meet short- and medium-term obligations.
EchoStar said it intends to seek recovery from News Corp for any costs of financing in excess of the costs of the financing expected through News Corp.

The admendment expands a May 8 suit, filed by EchoStar in the U.S. District Court for the District of Colorado. In that suit, it has sought a declaratory judgement confirming the obligations of News Corp to make the $200 million loan.
In February, News Corp agreed to pay $1 billion in cash and assets for a 50 percent stake in EchoStar.
Their venture, which was to offer up to 500 channels of digital TV, Internet services and local braodcast TV signals to U.S. markets, began to crumble not long after it was signed.
